key_insight: The paper learns Koopman embeddings directly from data with a kernel-based bilevel optimization framework, avoiding the need to predefine a dictionary.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more interpretable and scalable alternative to neural autoencoder approaches for forecasting and reduced-order modeling of nonlinear dynamical systems.
method: EDMD-kDL combines kernel dictionaries with extended dynamic mode decomposition.
A bilevel optimization scheme jointly learns the embedding and Koopman approximation.
Collocation-based formulation keeps kernel matrix size tied to collocation points, improving scalability.
evidence_signal: Across experiments on sea-surface-temperature forecasting and video data, EDMD-kDL matches or outperforms ANN-based methods.
watch_item: Performance depends on choosing suitable kernels, collocation points, and optimization settings, which may affect robustness and implementation complexity.
paper_title: Bilevel optimization for data-driven learning of Koopman embeddings using kernel-based autoencoders
